header: L6 · The test architect who has seen coverage lie · sonnet
verdict: Round-12 findings L6-r12-1, L6-r12-2 and the spec half of L6-r12-3 read as resolved; the delta adds a solid I17 test for fingerprint-unstable, with one boundary left untested (the fourth consecutive changed-fingerprint rerun) and the new (c) and (e) T005 bullets having no named red fixture for (e).

findings.defect: RJ-338 fires on 'the salvage a changed fingerprint started is the third in a row', and the I17 test covers reruns one to three and the recovery; no case says what the fourth rerun does after an exit 5 left three fingerprint-changed entries as the newest (exit 5 again, or a new salvage that counts as the fourth).
findings.scenario: An implementation tests 'count == 3'; after the exit 5 the writer keeps running, the fourth rerun counts four, passes the equality, and salvages without limit; the I17 test stays green because it stops at the third.
findings.change: State the rule as 'three or more' in 04 4.4 and add to the I17 case a fourth rerun with the writer still running that exits 5 again; the removal that turns it red is comparing the count with equality.

findings.defect: Requirement (e), the same surface set from every committed ask-first.yaml and grants.yaml for pr and the generator, is 'held by a test, or both use one reader', yet unlike (b) and the 12.4 fixtures it names no fixture and no removal that turns it red.
findings.scenario: The test compares only the surface ids and not the globs, or the two readers diverge on a glob; the test passes while pr and the generator disagree on which paths a surface covers.
findings.change: Name the fixture pair (two files with the same ids and different globs fail; identical files pass) and the removal of the comparison that turns the first red, or state that one reader is the choice and the test then asserts a single call site.

findings.section: plan T005 acceptance (c) go.work, go.work.sum, vendor/
findings.defect: The refusal of a tracked go.work, go.work.sum or vendor/ has 'one fixture each' but no stated removal that turns each red and no case for a head that already tracks the file at the base (add versus already present).
findings.scenario: The check is written against the head tree only and flags a base that legitimately tracks vendor/, or is written against the diff only and misses a head that keeps a base file; fixtures for 'adds' pass either way.
findings.change: State whether the refusal is 'head tracks' or 'head adds', give the fixture for the other case, and name the removal (the path pattern per file) that turns each fixture red.
